state_legend.label: answered
state_legend.meaning: The source replied and returned records.

state_legend.label: answered, zero
state_legend.meaning: The source replied and genuinely had nothing. A quiet field, not a fault.

state_legend.label: answered in part
state_legend.meaning: The source answered every page; resmon stopped at its own time budget or the run's cap.

state_legend.label: could not be asked
state_legend.meaning: No key, retired, no author query, or a window the source cannot answer.

state_legend.label: failed
state_legend.meaning: The source was asked and the exchange broke.

state_legend.label: outcome not recorded
state_legend.meaning: resmon did not observe an outcome. This is not a success and not a failure.

state_legend.label: not asked on this run
state_legend.meaning: This run's saved selection did not name this source. Nothing was asked of it.

verdict.headline: CORE and DBLP have not answered any run resmon has a record of.
detail: Crossref, DOAJ, EuropePMC, HAL, OpenAlex, PLOS, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and Zenodo answered when last asked and are no longer in the most recent run's saved selection.

notes: Every cell is one source's recorded answer to one run. Nothing here is inferred: a run with no row for a source reads as not recorded.
A source that answered and whose records resmon could not store reads as answered, because the source did reply with records. The cell's note carries how many were matched and how many were kept.

Answered in part is resmon stopping, at its own time budget or the run's cap, not the source failing. The cell's note says which part of the window was read; the rest was not read and is counted neither way.
A cancelled run reads as not recorded for every source it was still querying: resmon observed its own cancellation, not an answer.
Not asked and not recorded are different marks. The first is a choice saved on the run; the second is a gap in what resmon observed.
